parameters.content:
PURPOSE
Main intake workflow. Webhook -> validate -> normalize -> opt-out check -> dedupe -> AI qualify -> score -> CRM upsert -> AI draft -> AUTO_SEND (send-then-verify) or HUMAN_APPROVAL (token + link, real send happens in workflow 4).
Companion workflows: 02 Follow-up Processor, 03 Reply Detector, 04 Approval & Send.

CRITICAL FIX: SEND-THEN-VERIFY
Gmail send nodes use onError=continueErrorOutput, giving two outputs: 0=success, 1=failure.
CRM is marked CONTACTED / First Contacted At / Next Follow-up At ONLY on output 0.
On output 1 (failure): status is left untouched, failure is logged to Errors with Severity=CRITICAL, and the owner is alerted with the draft so they can send manually.

CONFIGURATION
Edit 'Config (EDIT ME)': OWNER_EMAIL, BOOKING_URL, GOOGLE_SHEET_ID/NAME, ERROR_SHEET_NAME, MODE, TIMEZONE (e.g. Asia/Kolkata), FOLLOW_UP_1/2/3_DAYS, AI_MODEL, SENDER_EMAIL, N8N_BASE_URL, APPROVE_SEND_PATH.
Credentials: Google Sheets OAuth2, Gmail OAuth2, Anthropic API.

APPROVAL MECHANISM
HUMAN_APPROVAL generates a random single-use token, persists {Draft Subject, Draft Body, Approval Token, Status=PENDING_APPROVAL} to the sheet FIRST, then emails the owner a magic link to workflow 4's webhook (leadId+token). Nothing is sent to the lead here.
See SETUP_GUIDE.md 'How the owner approves a draft'.

parameters.content:
PURPOSE
Runs daily. Scans the Leads sheet for any lead due a follow-up, generates a short AI follow-up, sends it, and reschedules - all gated on a confirmed successful send.

FIX: NON-COMPOUNDING SCHEDULE
Next Follow-up At is always computed as First Contacted At (Day 0) + the configured day offset for the UPCOMING follow-up - never 'now + offset'.
Day 0 send -> FU1 Day 1 -> FU2 Day 3 -> FU3 Day 7. Confirmed NOT Day 1 -> Day 4 -> Day 11.
Timezone-aware via Luxon DateTime.setZone(config.timezone), with a plain-Date fallback.

STOP CONDITIONS
Status in [REPLIED, CLOSED, NOT_INTERESTED, MEETING_BOOKED, CONVERTED] -> stop.
Reply Detected=TRUE or Opted Out=TRUE -> stop.
Follow-up Count >= maxFollowUps -> stop.
No First Contacted At anchor, no Email, or Next Follow-up At empty/future -> not due.
Status NEW/QUALIFIED/PENDING_APPROVAL -> not this workflow's job.

nodes.notes: Polls the inbox. The 'q' filter already excludes Sent and Drafts at the Gmail API level (fix: was '-in:sent -in:draft', corrected to Gmail's actual label syntax '-in:sent -in:drafts'); the code below adds a second belt-and-suspenders self-mail check in case a message still arrives with the client's own address as sender (e.g. an auto-forward).

nodes.notes: Extracts sender, thread ID (when the Gmail Trigger node exposes it), and message timestamp. If any field is missing the corresponding check below is skipped rather than causing a crash - see the 'Limitations' sticky note.

nodes.name: Not Self-Sent?
nodes.notes: Ignores mail sent by the business's own outreach address or the owner's address (e.g. a Sent-then-synced copy, an internal CC, or an owner reply-all) so it's never mistaken for a lead reply.

nodes.name: Evaluate Reply Confidence
nodes.notes: This is the false-positive reduction logic requested in the audit. Kept intentionally simple (status + timing, with thread-id as a confidence booster only) rather than full email-thread parsing, to stay reliable - see Limitations sticky.

nodes.name: End - Not a Genuine Reply
nodes.notes: Covers: unknown sender, lead never contacted (NEW/QUALIFIED/PENDING_APPROVAL), lead already REPLIED/CLOSED/etc, or the message predates our outreach. No sheet write, no owner notification - avoids noisy false alarms.

They may still receive an automated follow-up. Please update the sheet row manually right away (Status=REPLIED, Reply Detected=TRUE, Next Follow-up At=blank).

parameters.content:
PURPOSE
Polls the inbox for new mail. If the sender matches a lead that is actually mid-sequence (CONTACTED/FOLLOW_UP_1-3) and the message timing is consistent with that sequence, marks REPLIED, clears Next Follow-up At, and alerts the owner.

FALSE-POSITIVE REDUCTION
1. Ignore mail from the business's own sender/owner address.
2. Require the lead to be in an active sequence (not NEW/QUALIFIED/PENDING_APPROVAL and not already REPLIED/CLOSED/etc).
3. Require the message timestamp to be on/after Last Contacted At (minus a 5-min clock-skew grace) - filters out an old unrelated email from before outreach began.
4. If a stored Last Thread Id matches the incoming message's thread, confidence is HIGH_THREAD_MATCH; otherwise MEDIUM (still treated as genuine) - thread mismatch alone never blocks a reply.

LIMITATIONS (documented, not hidden)
- Gmail Trigger's exposed fields (thread ID, precise headers) vary by n8n/Gmail-node version; thread matching is a confidence signal, not a hard gate, specifically because it can't be relied on 100% of the time.
- This does not parse email body content or use NLP to detect 'not interested' vs a genuine reply - ANY reply from an in-sequence lead is treated the same way (REPLIED, sequence stopped), which is deliberately conservative: a human then reviews it.
- A lead who replies from a different email address than the one on file will not be matched.

nodes.name: Approval Webhook
nodes.notes: GET so the owner can approve by clicking a link in the notification email (a magic link, like a common unsubscribe/confirm pattern). Query params: leadId, token. See SETUP_GUIDE.md 'How the owner approves a draft' for the security model and its limits.

parameters.jsCode: const webhook=$('Approval Webhook').item.json;const body=webhook.body||{};const leadId=String(body.leadId||'').trim();const token=String(body.approvalToken||'').trim();return [{json:{...$json,leadId,token}}];

const req=$('Extract leadId + token').item.json; const row=$json; const reasons=[]; const found=!!(row&&row['Lead ID']&&String(row['Lead ID'])===req.leadId); if(!found) reasons.push('no lead found for this leadId'); let tokenOk=false,expiryOk=false; if(found){ try { const crypto=require('crypto'); if(!crypto||typeof crypto.timingSafeEqual!=='function') throw new Error('SECURE_CRYPTO_UNAVAILABLE'); const stored=String(row['Approval Token Hash']||''); const actual=crypto.createHash('sha256').update(String(req.token||''),'utf8').digest('hex'); tokenOk=/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/i.test(stored)&&crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(stored,'hex'),Buffer.from(actual,'hex')); } catch(e) { tokenOk=false; reasons.push('secure token validation unavailable'); } if(!tokenOk) reasons.push('token missing, already used, or does not match'); const ms=Date.parse(row['Approval Token Expires At']||''); expiryOk=Number.isFinite(ms)&&Date.now()<ms; if(!expiryOk) reasons.push('approval token expired or expiry missing/invalid'); } let statusOk=false,optedOut=false,replied=false; if(found){const status=(row.Status||'').toUpperCase();statusOk=status==='PENDING_APPROVAL';if(!statusOk)reasons.push('lead is no longer pending approval');optedOut=String(row['Opted Out']||'FALSE').toUpperCase()==='TRUE';if(optedOut)reasons.push('lead has opted out');replied=String(row['Reply Detected']||'FALSE').toUpperCase()==='TRUE';if(replied)reasons.push('lead has already replied');} const hasEmail=found&&!!row.Email;if(found&&!hasEmail)reasons.push('lead has no email on file'); const eligible=found&&tokenOk&&expiryOk&&statusOk&&!optedOut&&!replied&&hasEmail; const draftSubject=row['Draft Subject']||'';const draftBody=row['Draft Body']||'';return [{json:{config:req.config,leadId:req.leadId,row,eligible,reasons,hasDraft:!!(draftSubject&&draftBody),draftSubject,draftBody}}];

parameters.content:
PURPOSE
Completes the HUMAN_APPROVAL loop from workflow 1. The owner clicks a per-lead magic link (leadId+token) from the approval email. This workflow re-validates eligibility, sends the stored (or safely regenerated) draft, and ONLY on confirmed Gmail success advances the lead to CONTACTED with a scheduled follow-up.

HOW THE OWNER APPROVES A DRAFT
1. Workflow 1 generates a random single-use token and stores {Draft Subject, Draft Body, Approval Token} on the lead's row.
2. The owner receives an email with a link: {n8nBaseUrl}/webhook/approve-send?leadId=...&token=...
3. Clicking it calls this workflow (GET), which checks the token matches AND the lead is still PENDING_APPROVAL AND not opted-out/replied, then sends.
4. The token is cleared after a successful send (single-use) so the link can't be replayed to send twice.
SECURITY NOTE: this is a magic-link pattern (like an unsubscribe link), not enterprise auth - suitable for a solo agency's owner-only approval flow. Do not forward the approval email. For extra hardening, restrict the /webhook/approve-send path at the reverse-proxy/firewall level to the owner's IP if that's practical for the deployment.

parameters.content:
ELIGIBILITY RE-CHECK
The approval token is SHA-256 hashed in Sheets and the transactional database. At POST time, a conditional database update requires matching token hash, pending state, unexpired token, and no reply/opt-out. A unique outbox claim enforces one successful consumer; opening the GET confirmation page does not send.

parameters.content:
TRANSACTIONAL OUTBOX DELIVERY
Atomic PostgreSQL claims stop concurrent approvals, auto sends and follow-up sends. Approval bearer values are hashed before storage. A confirmed send is marked SENT only after the provider returns success. Any Gmail error with an uncertain outcome is marked UNKNOWN and is not retried automatically; reconcile provider delivery before manual recovery. Explicit provider rejection can enter bounded backoff retry.
